question_text:
A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of worsening fever, headache, photophobia, and nausea for 2 days. One week ago, she returned from summer camp. She has received all age-appropriate immunizations. Her temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F). She is oriented to person, place, and time. Physical examination shows a maculopapular rash. There is rigidity of the neck; forced flexion of the neck results in involuntary flexion of the knees and hips. Cerebrospinal fluid studies show:
Opening pressure 120 mm H2O
Appearance Clear
Protein 47 mg/dL
Glucose 68 mg/dL
White cell count 280/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 15%
Lymphocytes 85%
Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?"?

                    ### Question
                    A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of worsening fever, headache, photophobia, and nausea for 2 days. One week ago, she returned from summer camp. She has received all age-appropriate immunizations. Her temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F). She is oriented to person, place, and time. Physical examination shows a maculopapular rash. There is rigidity of the neck; forced flexion of the neck results in involuntary flexion of the knees and hips. Cerebrospinal fluid studies show:
Opening pressure 120 mm H2O
Appearance Clear
Protein 47 mg/dL
Glucose 68 mg/dL
White cell count 280/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 15%
Lymphocytes 85%
Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?"?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Echovirus
opb. Listeria monocytogenes
opc. Herpes simplex virus

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The clinical presentation of fever, headache, photophobia, nausea, neck rigidity, and a maculopapular rash, along with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings of clear appearance, high lymphocyte count, normal glucose, and elevated protein, is consistent with viral meningitis. The high percentage of lymphocytes (85%) and normal glucose levels in the CSF strongly suggest a viral rather than bacterial cause. Among the viral causes, Echovirus is a common cause of viral meningitis, especially in children and adolescents, and is associated with summer outbreaks, aligning with the patient's recent return from summer camp. Herpes simplex virus is less likely given the typical presentation and epidemiology. Bacterial causes such as Listeria monocytogenes, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Neisseria meningitidis are unlikely due to the CSF profile, which would typically show a higher neutrophil count and lower glucose levels. Therefore, the most likely causal organism is Echovirus.
